page: Amazon Web Services c6i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 54 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support spans AVX-512 extensions including AVX512_VNNI, alongside dedicated cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags.

Network infrastructure provides a baseline throughput of 19 Gbps, while the instance features no bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS. In benchmark testing, the processor shows solid mid-tier compute capabilities, recording 46,465.78 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,737.0. Hardware-assisted cryptography tests place in the top 25% with a PassMark encryption score of 42,481.53, and image processing also ranks in the top quartile at 15,272.0 on Geekbench.

Memory throughput reaches 165.37 GB/s for large uncached reads and 68.06 GB/s for large writes, reflecting standard dual-channel DDR4 behavior. Web and data serving benchmarks reflect steady throughput, with static web delivery at 39.43 GB/s and Redis processing reaching 43.43 million SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference handles smaller models adequately, such as 243.51 tokens per second on a 135M model, but drops to a lower-tier 2.79 tokens per second when generating text on a 70B parameter model due to lack of discrete GPU acceleration.

The 2:1 memory-to-core ratio delivers efficient compute resource density for CPU-bound tasks without surplus memory overhead. AWS c6i.12xlarge is well matched for scalable compute workloads, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application serving pools, batch processing, and cryptographic microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, paired with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, adhering to a 2:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators such as VAES and SHA-NI, which yield top-quartile performance in encryption and image processing tests. The instance operates without bundled local storage and connects via a 19 Gbps network interface. Benchmark results show consistent mid-tier throughput across multi-core compute, web serving at 39.43 GB/s, and Redis handling 43.43 million SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators, large-model LLM generation drops sharply. The server serves effectively in distributed compute, software compilation, batch processing, and network edge-serving architectures.
